signature.name: Royal Palace of Cambodia
signature.detail: The official residence of the King and the city's most iconic sight, with the Silver Pagoda inside its walls. Go early in the morning to avoid heat and crowds; tickets are around $10 and shoulders and knees must be covered.

signature.name: Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum
signature.detail: A former school turned prison and interrogation center under the Khmer Rouge, now a sobering museum. Visit with a guide or audio tour for context; allow 1-2 hours and go early to avoid the heat.

signature.name: Killing Field
signature.detail: The Choeung Ek memorial site, where thousands were executed, is a deeply moving place with a stupa of skulls. It is about 30 minutes by tuk-tuk from the center; combine with Tuol Sleng for a full understanding of Cambodia's recent history.

signature.name: Silver Pagoda
signature.detail: Located within the Royal Palace grounds, this temple houses a floor of silver tiles and a revered emerald Buddha. Dress respectfully (no shorts or sleeveless tops) and visit in the morning when it is cooler.

signature.name: Wat Phnom
signature.detail: The city's namesake hilltop temple, a peaceful spot with good views and a lively atmosphere with monkeys and locals. It is a short walk from the riverside; go early morning or late afternoon.

signature.name: National Museum of Cambodia
signature.detail: Houses the world's finest collection of Khmer art, including sculptures from Angkor. The building itself is a beautiful example of Khmer architecture; a guide or audio tour is recommended.

signature.name: Mekong River
signature.detail: The mighty Mekong is central to Phnom Penh's identity, with lively riverfront promenades and sunset cruises. Take a boat trip at sunset for great views of the city skyline.

signature.name: Independence Monument of Cambodia
signature.detail: A striking monument in the heart of the city, especially beautiful when illuminated at night. It is a short walk from the Royal Palace and a good spot for photos.
